items.text: Videos released show that the birthday ceremony of Sepehr Esmaeili, a young man killed during the Mahsa uprising, was held with the presence of the mothers of the martyrs Nazanin Esmikani and Mohammad Fateh beside his grave. Sepehr Esmaeili, on 24 Aban 1401 and on his 21st birthday, was heading to Zibakenar with friends and relatives when checkpoint officers opened fire on the car with Kalashnikovs without warning or alert.

The United Nations Security Council will hold a public meeting on Friday at Bahrain's request to discuss rising tensions in the Persian Gulf region. A main focus of the meeting is reviewing the implementation of Resolution 2817, which condemns attacks by the Islamic Republic on Gulf countries. The meeting will also discuss threats to maritime security and the risk of renewed military conflicts with the Islamic Republic.

Conservative members in the Canadian Parliament's immigration committee proposed an emergency plan for the immediate expulsion of Islamic Republic officials from the country. These members asked Mark Carney's government to amend immigration laws to ban the entry of Islamic Republic agents and their families into Canada and to publicly disclose the names of recognized officials of this regime.

Judicial sources in Lebanon reported ongoing investigations into five Hezbollah members who were arrested between Batroun and Bsharri in northern Lebanon. Initial findings indicate these individuals were surveying and examining the area. Judicial sources suspect this mission had security or military objectives or was related to establishing a base in the region.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing a missile in the streets of Tehran and said they saw it on the evening of 21 Aban in Tajrish Square.

Several young artists in Ahvaz have designed and decorated the bodies of a Dodge Challenger and a Nissan Z inspired by the video game GTA 6. They then showcased their cars by performing drifting moves and captured the results on film.

Alexey Likhachov, CEO of Rosatom, said the company currently sees no risk of slowing down its activities at the Bushehr nuclear power plant and intends to increase the number of Russian specialists there from 180 to 300. He added that Rosatom plans to restore the pace of work and number of staff to the planned level next year. There is also an agreement with Iran to build large nuclear power plants and small nuclear units, currently in the planning and design stage.

Data from the IQAir live air pollution monitoring website shows that Tehran is the second most polluted city in the world today. Statistics indicate that thousands of people in Iran die annually due to diseases caused by air pollution, but serious and sufficient actions by officials to address this crisis are not observed.

A video shows that the birthday ceremony of the late Reza Karimi was held on Thursday, 21 Aban, with the presence of families seeking justice at his grave. Reza Karimi, 50 years old, was killed on 19 Dey 1404 in the Malekshahr neighborhood of Isfahan.
The police commander of Kohgiluyeh County reported the arrest of 10 citizens in this county on charges described as "security crimes."

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, confirmed that the Islamic Republic threatened him with death. He said cabinet members are not afraid of these threats and consider them a sign of the success of the US economic pressure campaign. Bessent likened the Revolutionary Guards to a "dangerous animal trapped."

The Iranian Writers' Association announced that five journalists and poets from Abadan were tried again on charges of "spreading lies" and "participating in illegal gatherings." Their court session was held on 18 Aban. The case lawyer said the retrial violates the principle of double jeopardy and the court should be held with a jury.

A video sent to Iran International shows the flower-covered grave of Alireza Sepahi in Kashan. He was the fugitive accused in the "Ali Khani Square Isfahan" case who was executed at dawn on Tuesday, 13 Mehr, in Dastgerd Prison, Isfahan.

Kaveh Kurdestani, a resident of Mariwan, was arrested by security forces on 12 Aban. After eight days of interrogation and detention in a security detention center in Tehran, he was transferred to Greater Tehran Prison.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations announced that 42% of ships currently on the Islamic Republic's "non-compliance" list have been involved in maritime incidents in the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, and the Sea of Oman. The report covers regional events from the start of the war on 9 Esfand 1404 to 20 Aban 1405. Seven attacks on oil tankers were recorded in the seven days leading to 20 Aban, and the threat level in the Strait of Hormuz remains "severe."
The head of the judiciary in Semnan province reported that the complainant has pardoned the execution of the amputation sentence in one of the judicial cases in this province.

British police released a video of the arrest of two Iranian men accused of spying for Iran. These two were hired by an intelligence agency of the Islamic Republic to monitor Iranian journalists and a lawyer. Mostafa Sepahvand and Farhad Javadi-Mansh were found guilty after a six-week trial at Woolwich Court in London for activities that could assist a foreign intelligence service.
It was reported that the US Army sent an important message to the Israeli Army. It was also reported that the head of Mossad traveled secretly to Washington and Miami.
A video received by Iran International shows a citizen pointing to a long gasoline queue in Manoujan, Kerman. The citizen says the length of the gas station queue reached about five kilometers.

Farhikhtegan newspaper reported that the officials of the Football Federation Referees Committee are looking for the person who leaked the audio file of the referees' conversations from the Esteghlal Khuzestan vs Esteghlal match to the media. This audio file revealed the insults of Alireza Ildarom, the assistant referee, towards Yaser Asani, Esteghlal's star player. Officials have warned that if the leaker is identified, they will deal with them seriously.

Last week, reports covered illegal wildlife hunting and trapping, wood smuggling, air pollution in Khuzestan, Isfahan, Mashhad, and Tehran, water scarcity and drying wetlands, and tree drying in Tehran parks. Over 160 tons of smuggled wood were discovered in Talesh and Lahijan, and unhealthy air was recorded at stations in several cities. Additionally, 10 polluting units were sealed, 9 charcoal kilns destroyed, 60% drying of Hoor al-Azim wetland, and 86% emptiness of South Khorasan dams were reported.

The Islamic Republic News Agency, IRNA, reported on the evening of Friday, 22 Aban that an explosion sound was heard in Jask, but no injuries were reported in the area. Meanwhile, the Hormozgan governor's office stated that no impact or explosion has been reported in the province.

A video received shows that a group of citizens in Bandar Abbas on the evening of Friday, 22 Aban, protested the lack of gasoline by parking their cars on Rajaei Highway and in front of the Aftab Derakhshan fuel station, blocking the street.

Iranian media quoted Ali Pourmand, head of the medical committee of Tehran Football Board, saying that due to increased pollution levels and the risk of sports activities, all football activities in Tehran province will not take place on Saturday, 23 Aban 1405 [Gregorian: 2026-11-14].

On Friday, 22 Aban, several prisoners in Tehran's Great Prison were beaten after protesting against the treatment of one of their fellow inmates by the guards. Amirhossein Dastjerdi was injured in the chest but was not transferred to the infirmary. Additionally, two political prisoners named Moein Najafi and Ramin Joonaki were moved to solitary confinement, with one of them returned to the ward after a few hours.

A citizen sent a voice message to Iran International reporting a severe shortage of gasoline in Shiraz, Fasa, Bandar Abbas, and other cities, stating that free gasoline is only available for a few hours in the morning at many stations. The citizen added that after about two hours of waiting in line, he was told the gasoline was finished, and a station official mentioned the possibility of removing free cards and limiting quotas.

It was reported that at least six Iranian athletes are on the verge of execution by the Islamic Republic. Soraya Aghaei and Kaveh Mehrabi, Iran's representatives in the International Olympic Committee, have not made efforts to support these athletes. This issue was raised in an interview with Mehdi Rostampour, a sports journalist.

Sharren Haskell, former Israeli Deputy Foreign Minister, said the difference between Benjamin Netanyahu's and Gadi Eizenkot's foreign and security policies is very small, and both consider the IRGC a serious threat to Israel. He added that if the Islamic Republic remains, it will regain power and arm itself, and confronting it in the future will be more costly.

Reports from Karaj indicate that due to economic recession, people cannot afford purchases and mostly buy on credit, resulting in debt to the government. In Tabriz, it was reported that Ata Airlines has not paid staff salaries for four months and employees face threats of dismissal. Also, in Gilan province, welfare payments for retired airline workers have been unpaid since Bahman 1404, and insurance costs are paid with delays.

Sky News reported that US Army forces stationed at the RAF Lakenheath airbase reacted on Friday evening to unauthorized suspicious drone activity. A US Air Force spokesperson stated that no personnel, aircraft, or infrastructure were damaged.

Pouria Nazemi, a science journalist, said a widespread disruption in Microsoft services that affected millions of users and several government agencies and companies worldwide was likely caused by technical problems in updating the company's infrastructure. According to him, disruption in communication between servers and transferring load to healthy servers caused services like Outlook and Teams to become unavailable. Nazemi added that although most Microsoft services have been restored, some services have not yet returned to normal operation and warned that the risk of cyberattacks during international crises increases the need to strengthen backup systems.

Jassim Al-Budaiwi, Secretary-General of the Gulf Cooperation Council, called on the UN Security Council to require the Islamic Republic to pay full compensation for the damages caused by its attacks on the council member states and to hold the perpetrators accountable. He said the member states have been targeted by over seven thousand missiles and drones from Iran since 9 Esfand 1404. Al-Budaiwi demanded the immediate and unconditional cessation of attacks by the Islamic Republic and its proxy forces and called for the implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 2817.

Jamal Faris Al-Ruwaie, Bahrain's permanent representative to the United Nations, said Gulf Cooperation Council member states must participate in any agreement or negotiation regarding regional security and stability. He called for a complete halt to attacks and threats by the Islamic Republic and accountability for the perpetrators. Al-Ruwaie said the council countries have been targeted by missile and drone attacks from the Islamic Republic and affiliated armed groups since 9 Esfand.

Jennifer Lokta, the US representative to the United Nations, called for joint action by Security Council members to hold the Islamic Republic accountable and said these measures should continue until Tehran complies with relevant resolutions. On Friday, November 13, she said at a Security Council meeting that the US stands with its partners in the Gulf against the Islamic Republic's efforts to undermine regional stability and supports Saudi Arabia against attacks by Iran-backed Houthis. Lokta also accused the Houthis of imposing illegal restrictions on ship movements in Bab al-Mandab and said they have besieged the city of Taiz, causing hunger and displacement for hundreds of thousands.

The FlightAware website reported that nearly 7,000 flights in the US were canceled or delayed following a nationwide flight halt order. The US Federal Aviation Administration issued this order due to communication disruptions at air traffic control centers. The US National Weather Service also announced it faced widespread internet and communication system disruptions.

Reza Talebi, a journalist, said that the disagreement among global powers and regional countries has prevented consensus in the UN Security Council to confront the actions of the Islamic Republic. According to him, China and Russia have limited legal actions against Tehran by using their veto power, which has emphasized the role of regional agreements and bilateral relations. Talebi added that if diplomatic and legal efforts reach a deadlock, Arab countries might participate as supporting forces in practical actions against the Islamic Republic within the framework of the US strategy.

Kambiz Tavana said that recent statements by Scott Bessent indicate Washington is no longer seeking an agreement similar to past negotiations with the Islamic Republic. The US now expects the Islamic Republic to take seven specific steps to show readiness for an agreement. Tavana added that Washington is focused on continuing economic and military pressure and will not change this approach until the Islamic Republic takes practical steps.

Shahram Kholdi said the trip of Roman Gafman, head of Mossad, to Washington is aimed at influencing Donald Trump's decisions about the Islamic Republic. He mentioned the possibility of a trilateral meeting between the leaders of the US, Russia, and China, as well as internal political developments in Israel, affecting security and military decisions. Kholdi added that intensifying sanctions can weaken the governance capacity of the Islamic Republic but is not sufficient for its collapse, and a short-term military operation might also be necessary.

A widespread disruption in Microsoft services has entered its second day, affecting user access to the company's services worldwide. Microsoft stated it is closer to fully restoring services but has no specific time for all services to return to normal. The disruption began on Thursday and has impacted services like Outlook, Microsoft Teams, and Copilot.

Following a widespread disruption in air traffic control communications and a nationwide flight halt in the US, reports indicate a gradual restoration of communication services and issuance of takeoff permissions at some airports in the country. The Wall Street Journal, citing informed sources, reported that communications at some US air traffic control centers are gradually returning to normal. San Francisco International Airport announced that flights to Hawaii and Asia are permitted to take off.

The US Federal Aviation Administration announced that the nationwide order to stop outgoing flights has been canceled following the resolution of a communication disruption. This decision was made after the traffic control radars went down.

Ali Al-Zaidi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, ordered an investigation into the oil smuggling network in the Jurf al-Sakhar area, the base of Kata'ib Hezbollah, a militia group close to the Islamic Republic. At the same time, military operations to besiege this area have been temporarily halted.

A passenger ship carrying about 190 passengers docked at the Mississippi River port in New Orleans, Louisiana, sank after colliding with an oil tanker. The mayor of New Orleans said 32 passengers were taken to local hospitals with non-serious injuries. The American Red Cross and the National Transportation Safety Board are present at the scene and are providing aid.

Ali Ehsassi, a Liberal member of the Canadian Federal Parliament, said that case-by-case review of the files of the IRGC conscript soldiers is not an effective solution and causes a lot of pressure and stress on their families.

Omid Shokri, a senior researcher at George Mason University, said that high consumption of low-quality vehicles, aging transportation fleet, sanctions, and organized gasoline smuggling are factors in the gasoline shortage in provinces like Hormozgan. He added that there are reports of an eight-billion-dollar income from gasoline smuggling for government agencies. He also said that the continued imbalance in the energy industry and weak distribution infrastructure have contributed to fuel shortages and citizen protests.

Reza Goharzad said the G7 statement on the Islamic Republic is drafted to somewhat align the views of the US and European countries. He emphasized that preventing the Islamic Republic from obtaining nuclear weapons and cooperating with the International Atomic Energy Agency remain key points of the West's common stance. Issues such as missile programs, proxy group activities, and regional maritime security also matter in US and European calculations.

Alireza Mahdavi, deputy of the Non-Communicable Diseases Management Center of the Ministry of Health, said that the population of people with diabetes and prediabetes in Iran reaches about 20 million. He added that childhood obesity, physical inactivity, and increased screen time are factors contributing to the rise in type 2 diabetes among children and adolescents. He also noted a decrease in the age of onset of type 2 diabetes, with cases now seen among teenagers.

Farhad Bashiri, a representative of Pakdasht in the parliament, said the recent events show the need for more efforts to reveal the hidden face and deceptive discourse of the US. He added that serious disagreements and lack of coordination are observed among US government officials, including Trump and his vice president. Bashiri also said that the events in the US congressional elections forced Trump to admit that the American people have not accepted war and express hatred towards Israel.

Alaeddin Boroujerdi, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said that the blood of their leader must be avenged against the US and Israel, but the positive developments and capacities formed after the enemy's aggression should not be overlooked. He added that despite the damages suffered in the war, these developments have brought important achievements in military, political, national power, and social cohesion. Boroujerdi also said that the Islamic Republic's capabilities in air defense and air offense will definitely transform.

Associated Press reported that contradictory statements by Donald Trump about Iran after the US midterm elections have cast uncertainty over the prospects of war and negotiations with Tehran. Trump said it is unlikely that new attacks against Iran will be needed and stated that the US no longer needs a deal with Tehran. Qatar continues efforts to reach a temporary agreement to resume ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, but Trump's recent positions have cast doubt on this process.

Mostafa Danandeh has reported that fuel carriers are citizens in deprived areas of Iran facing many economic and social problems and are not included in the "Organization and Supervision of Border Trade" law. This law, passed in Bahman 1402, has set procedures for kolbari and sailor trades but does not cover fuel carrying. Fuel carrying in Sistan and Baluchestan is linked to the specific economic and security conditions of the region and requires a policy suited to those conditions.

Mostafa Rajabi-Mashhadi, Deputy Minister of Electricity and Energy, told ILNA that fuel supply for power plants this winter will be more difficult than in previous years because 130 million cubic meters of the country's gas capacity are lost daily due to the war. He mentioned a 400 million cubic meter gas deficit and said the Ministry of Energy is trying to compensate for this shortage through consumption management and savings. The use of mazut as an alternative fuel will continue but will not increase compared to last year.

Esmaeil Safiri, head of the Football Federation referees committee, said the conflict in the match between Esteghlal Khuzestan and Esteghlal Tehran was an exceptional case that will not happen again. He said he does not know who insulted first. Safiri also defended Alireza Ildarom and said referees' conversations are recorded in VAR matches.

A report on living conditions under political repression and military tensions has been presented. Price increases, internet problems, and financial pressures on families are among the issues raised. Concerns about the future and difficult living conditions have been expressed.

The head of Mossad has traveled to Washington on the orders of Benjamin Netanyahu to discuss the possibility of resuming military attacks on the Islamic Republic. Axios reported that the goal of this trip is to persuade Donald Trump to resume the war. This report was made by Ashkan Safaei, a reporter for Iran International.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said that the weakening of the Islamic Republic and its proxy forces has created the conditions for a new regional alignment. He added that Turkey is trying to increase its geopolitical influence by expanding military and security cooperation with Qatar and to balance against the expansion of Israeli influence.

Abulfazl Mojarradi, a citizen from Bojnord, remains in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad in uncertainty after about six months of detention. He faces the charge of "Moharebeh" and no court session has been held for his case so far. According to Harana News Agency, he is still held in prison and no court session has been conducted to review his case.

Tasnim news agency reported on Saturday, 23 Aban, that the Islamic Republic technically has the capability to increase the range of its missiles beyond the 2,000-kilometer limit. The agency wrote that reducing the warhead weight of the "Khorramshahr 4" missile could extend its range to 3,000 to 4,000 kilometers, enabling targeting of US bases and allies in parts of Europe. Tasnim also stated that hitting the US East Coast requires a missile with about a 10,000-kilometer range, and covering the entire US territory needs a range over 13,000 kilometers, which is achievable using existing capacities in the IRGC's satellite launch programs.

Messages indicate that following the fuel crisis in Iran, long queues for gasoline have formed in some cities. Iran International has asked people to send videos, images, and their accounts about this problem.
Elina Hojati died on 18 Dey during public protests in Tehran due to shooting by Khamenei's forces. Her name remains in the memory of this land and her memory is a guiding light for freedom seekers.
On Tuesday, 19 Aban, Tareq Chakerzehi and Mansour Chakerzehi, two citizens from Nikshahr county, were arrested by security forces in this county and transferred to an unknown location.

Suspicious drones were observed over Lakenheath Air Base in eastern Britain, leading to a state of emergency and orders for American forces to take cover. The UK Ministry of Defence announced the end of the emergency, but joint investigations by British and American officials into the incident continue.

Masoumeh Taherkhani, an economic analyst, said the ultimate goal of the gradual increase in gasoline prices policy is to eliminate fuel subsidies and increase government revenue. She emphasized that pricing gasoline based on the dollar rate, while people's income is in rials, increases inflationary pressure on goods and services, and the cost of this policy is ultimately paid by the people.

Reza Shekari, former Persepolis and current Paykan player, reported threats against himself and his family by a person claiming affiliation with security agencies. He said this person made harsh demands regarding his personal and family matters and threatened to fabricate cases against him when questioned. Shekari has called for identifying the caller and legal follow-up by his lawyer.

Hossein Ali Hajideligani, deputy chairman of the Article 90 Commission of the parliament, said that one of the public demands is that the Islamic Republic should build and possess a nuclear bomb. He added that the use or non-use of this bomb is a matter to be decided at the appropriate time. He also said that due to Iran's vastness and the consequences of a nuclear attack, the enemy will not launch a nuclear attack.

Marco Materazzi, former Italy defender, reacted to the death of Jesus de Miguel by saying he is thankful that the incident did not happen to him. Jesus de Miguel died after colliding with the goalkeeper of the Andorra team in Spain's second division league. Materazzi also said that Zidane's headbutt in the 2006 World Cup final still bothers him after 20 years.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the link between revolutionary mentality and religious theology has made the Islamic Republic an unstable government. He added that when Washington concludes the Islamic Republic is non-negotiable, options such as overthrow and regime change will be considered.

Cyberattacks on cooling systems of stores in Europe have led to disagreements between Belgium's interior and foreign ministers about the role of the Islamic Republic. The interior minister considers Tehran's involvement very likely, but the foreign minister believes there is insufficient evidence to officially attribute the attacks to the Islamic Republic. Earlier, France accused the Revolutionary Guards of cyber sabotage in hundreds of stores.

A group of people protested the presence of women without hijab at Hamid Alidousti's funeral ceremony on Friday, 15 Aban, in front of the Jameh Mosque of Shahrak Gharb in Tehran. The attendees protested the participation of these women in the ceremony by chanting slogans against the presence of women without hijab.
It was reported that today, a kolbar was killed following gunfire by border forces in the border areas of Baneh.

Some citizens reported a shortage of gasoline in Shiraz and Fasa and the restriction of free gasoline distribution. Concerns about the removal of fuel cards at stations were also reported. Messages also indicate increased economic pressure and rising prices of essential goods.

Mohammad Ahmadi, the creator of the program "Dialogue Iran," has been sentenced to six months of suspended imprisonment and two years of prohibition from producing programs related to social issues. This sentence was issued after several court sessions. The news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Heshmatollah Falahatpisheh, former head of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said that the foreign policy of the Islamic Republic is one of the most mediated foreign policies in history and many national interests have been sacrificed due to collusion between mediators and other parties. He added that the cooling of mediation by countries such as Oman, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Qatar is a sign of diplomatic failure. Falahatpisheh also said that the Islamic Republic's reliance on mediators has led to the loss of a significant part of the country's diplomatic capacities.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, says the Trump administration still follows a "neither war nor agreement" strategy towards the Islamic Republic. He believes that continuing this situation could lead to war. Aghaei also pointed to the roles of Israel, China, and Russia in upcoming developments and the possibility of increased pressure to bring the Islamic Republic to the negotiating table.

Iran's national under-17 football team defeated Sri Lanka 11-0 in their second match of the Asian U-17 Championship qualifiers and topped Group D. The team played against Sri Lanka on Saturday, 23 Aban, at the National Stadium in Vientiane. Iran's youth team will face Jordan on Tuesday, 26 Aban.

The German parliament expanded the powers of the country's intelligence agencies to counter security threats and espionage activities by the Islamic Republic, Russia, and China by approving new reforms. These reforms allow covert entry into buildings with legal authorization and disruption of cyber systems of hackers affiliated with foreign governments.

According to a recent report by the Israeli research center Alma, the Islamic Republic currently possesses more than 1,700 ballistic missiles capable of reaching Israel. The institute stated that despite attacks on missile production infrastructure in Iran, Tehran has resumed efforts to rebuild its missile capabilities. Hossein Aghaei said that US and Israeli attacks have disrupted the Islamic Republic's missile production chain.

Ahmad Bakhshaish Ardestani, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said the possibility of war still exists unless negotiations can create an opening. He added that the US is trying to use a blockade to make people dissatisfied and weaken Iran so that people demand negotiations. Bakhshaish Ardestani also said the Islamic Republic has made it clear to the US that any attack on Iran will be met with a direct response against Israel.

The launch of the "Jan-Fada for Iran" campaign by an organization affiliated with the IRGC shows that the Islamic Republic is trying to rebuild the image of forces associated with repression using a new name and pave the way for recruiting new volunteers. The IRGC and Basij have become notorious institutions among a large part of Iranian society due to their direct role in suppressing protests and killing protesters over past decades and the national revolution of Dey 1404. The experience of authoritarian regimes in Syria and Venezuela shows that renaming and reorganizing security forces has precedent, but the "Jan-Fada" campaign in Iran uses a term that was employed by opponents of the Islamic Republic to commemorate those killed in the Dey protests.
Teddy Riner, a French judoka and five-time Olympic gold medalist, started his campaign for the 2027 French presidential election by visiting a hospital in the suburbs of Paris.

The Japan national football team defeated Brazil 3-2 in a friendly match. The game was held in the city of Kallang, Singapore. Rafinha and Carlo Ancelotti were sent off for protesting Japan's 90th-minute goal.

Reuters reported that Donald Trump told his advisors he might refrain from ordering new military attacks against Iran if Iran or Tehran-backed Houthis do not take provocative actions against the US. Trump is considering this possibility after meetings with national security advisors and intelligence reports but has not made a final decision. It was also reported that Saudi Arabia and Turkey have asked Trump not to resume military attacks against Iran.

Iran International audiences report increased security surveillance in schools, installation of cameras in classrooms, and pressure to comply with mandatory hijab. At the same time, families' concerns about inadequate heating and cold schools due to the energy crisis have made students' health and safety a worrying issue.

The public and revolutionary prosecutor of Mehriz County reported the closure of a cafe-garden in the mountainous areas of Miyankuh rural district. This business was closed by judicial order due to holding a ceremony described as inappropriate and contrary to legal regulations and social norms.

A recreational-sports complex named "Kourosh Sports Club" in Tonekabon was sealed by order of the public and revolutionary prosecutor of Tonekabon county. This action followed the release of a video showing several citizens present without observing mandatory hijab in the complex.

Reuters reported, citing two informed sources, that Donald Trump told Mohammed bin Salman in a phone call on 9 Aban that he intended to attack Iran after the US midterm elections. Mohammed bin Salman asked Trump to refrain from this action and said that economic sanctions against the Islamic Republic were yielding results. Reuters also reported that Mohammed bin Salman and Recep Tayyip Erdogan, in phone calls over the past two weeks, asked Trump not to resume military attacks against Iran.

Iranians residing in Sweden gathered again in Stockholm on Saturday, November 14, in the eleventh month of protests against the Islamic Republic, to commemorate Iran's martyrs and reflect the voices of protesters inside the country. A teenage girl participating in the gathering expressed support for Prince Reza Pahlavi and told Mehran Abbassian, a reporter for Iran International, "We will not leave the streets until Iran is free." Another participant held a photo of Mohammadreza Khani, an 18-year-old killed by Islamic Republic forces during the December protests in Karaj, saying, "It is a national duty to keep the memory of the martyrs alive as long as we live."

Tasnim reported that Alireza Beiranvand, a nominee for the 2026 Asian Footballer of the Year award, has obtained an exit permit to travel to Thailand and attend the Asian Football Awards ceremony despite serving his military service. The Asian Football Awards ceremony will be held on Thursday, 28 Aban in Bangkok. The AFC Secretary General invited Beiranvand and two other players to attend the ceremony.

The CEO of the Dairy Cooperatives Union announced that the price increase for milk has been approved and various dairy products will soon become more expensive. At the same time, a member of the Parliament's Economic Commission said the government has taken 10 million tomans from the people's pockets in exchange for one million tomans of ration coupons.

The head of the Central Bar Association announced that about 700 lawyers across the country faced legal action during the January 1404 protests. He said the issues of these individuals were resolved through negotiation and follow-up.

Reports of a 2-3 second tremor in East Tehran and areas including Narmak, Tehranpars, Shariati, and Hakimiyeh have been received. Some reports mention hearing a sound like something cracking underground before the tremor. This earthquake was reported at 17:43.
A video received by Iran International shows that Iranians in Denmark gathered in Copenhagen on Saturday to support the national revolution and commemorate the martyrs of Dey month.

Emmanuel Macron, President of France, arrived in Phnom Penh, the capital of Cambodia, on Saturday, 23 Aban, ahead of the Francophonie summit. Cambodia is the first destination of his trip to Southeast Asia. The trip will continue with his presence in Malaysia.

Mehdi Moslehi, an oil market expert, said there is a surplus of about two million barrels of oil supply and Gulf countries have been able to continue their exports through the Strait of Hormuz and alternative routes. He added that this trend is contrary to statements by Islamic Republic officials who said if Iran cannot sell oil, other countries in the region also cannot.

Abdolnaser Hemmati, the governor of the Central Bank, in response to Scott Bassett's threats about intensifying sanctions, said one should not judge the outcome prematurely and "count the chickens at the end of autumn." Hemmati said on Saturday, 23 Aban, on the sidelines of a government meeting that it is still early to talk about winter and added that nearly $30.3 billion in currency has been secured and the supply of currency for essential goods and medicine will continue.
